anya: Quick sanity-check: hydra embed bringup — seeing week-over-week cluster centroid drift on the news corpus after int6 quant. recall@10 drops ~2.4% vs fp16 on the most recent slice. Anyone seen temporal variance like this before? :thinking:

sam: which eval slices/dataset?

anya: internal-news-6m, split by week (wk0..wk23). Ran onnx int6 per-tensor fallback and fp16 baseline. Command I used:

```
# eval job
python eval_embeddings.py \n  --model hydra-v2-small \n  --quant int6_onnx \n  --dataset internal-news-6m \n  --split weekly \n  --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,centroid_shift
```

ravi: do you have numbers for multiple k? a 2.4% drop at k=10 might be noise if k=1/5 stable.

anya: quick paste from the run (aggregated):
- fp16: recall@1=0.512, @5=0.712, @10=0.792, silhouette=0.21
- int6: recall@1=0.505, @5=0.702, @10=0.768, silhouette=0.18
- centroid_shift (wk-to-wk avg L2): fp16=0.012, int6=0.018

toni: hmm centroid_shift difference stands out. Could be quant introducing small directional bias in embeddings. Did you zero-center per-batch or use global mean normalization?

anya: used global mean from training set, then L2 norm. No per-week re-centering.

sam: try computing week-wise mean and measure relative shift magnitude (norm of mean difference / mean norm). If shift aligns with particular weeks (e.g., recent news topics), that's data drift not quant.

mlbot: deploy-bot: new eval job queued for hydra-v2-small int6-perchannel with microbatch=64 by anya (job #8472).

anya: thanks. Also ran a small ensemble test: averaged embeddings from checkpoints t0,t2,t4 (fp16) vs int6-ensembled (quantize then average). Results:
- fp16-ensemble @10=0.804
- int6-then-average @10=0.779
- average-then-quantize @10=0.787

ravi: interesting ordering matters. average-then-quantize loses less than quantize-then-average. implies quantization noise isn't zero-mean across checkpoints.

toni: propose two followups: (1) run int6 per-channel calibration using a stratified weekly sample, (2) compute PCA of wk centroids to see if quant bias is along a few principal directions.

anya: on it. I'm spinning a PCA job and a per-channel calibration run. If PCA shows a dominant axis, we could apply a small debiasing projection before indexing.

sam: also check HNSW index sensitivity: re-indexing with ef_construction=256 vs 128 sometimes masks recall drops. Could be more robust search config covering quant noise.

anya: good call — will repro both reindex configs.

devops-bot: infra note: remember dedicated staging cluster has different GPU arithmetic; make sure the quant run used the same ONNX runtime flags as prod.

anya: confirmed same flags. Ran on staging-gpu-a (cuda 12, onnxruntime 1.15).

ravi: if per-channel calibration + PCA debias reduce centroid_shift but recall still lags, consider switching to int8-perchannel or fp16 for sensitive tiers. We can also try small temperature scaling on dot products during ranking (learned scalar) — sometimes compensates magnitude shrinkage.

anya: timeline: I'll post updated numbers by EOD. Current plan: 1) int6-perchannel calibration run, 2) PCA centroid axis check, 3) reindex ef test, 4) ensemble ordering experiment (avg->quant vs quant->avg).

toni: thanks — ping @sam @ravi when you have the EOD numbers. :thumbsup:

anya: quick interim result (18m later): int6-perchannel improved @10 from 0.768 -> 0.782, centroid_shift down to 0.013. PCA shows ~45% variance on first axis and quant bias projects heavily onto it. Reindex ef=256 gave +0.005 on recall@10 for int6 run.

sam: promising. If that's stable across 4 more weeks, we can include per-channel calibration in onboarding checklist and add a small debias step to the pipeline.

anya: will run 4-week rolling check. Thanks all.

ravi: nice work. If you want, I can help codify the calibration routine into the onboarding script.

anya: would love that. I'll drop the eval job ids and artifacts in the model-onboard ticket when done.
